findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it private to the VPC.
storage_encrypted = false means the RDS volume and its snapshots are stored unencrypted, exposing catalog data if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.
The master password is supplied from var.password in plaintext and is stored unencrypted in Terraform state; the username is also the default privileged 'admin' account.
The parameter group applied to this instance does not enforce require_secure_transport/SSL, so the application connects to MySQL in cleartext over the network.
The MySQL parameter group only sets character sets and omits require_secure_transport = 1, permitting unencrypted client connections to the database.

The EC2 user_data script interpolates the database master password (var.password) and username directly into the instance metadata, which is readable by anyone who can reach the IMDS endpoint or any process/SSRF vector on the instance, and is stored in plaintext in Terraform state.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with the credential-laden user_data and a web app, an SSRF could retrieve instance role credentials and the DB password.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's EBS volume (which holds the dbinfo.inc file containing the DB password) may be stored unencrypted.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing full control of all S3 buckets, EC2, and RDS in the account; compromise of the web server yields near-account-wide privileges.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic on all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised database host.
skip_final_snapshot = true with no deletion_protection means the database can be destroyed without any recoverable copy, enabling destructive data loss by anyone with API access.
The database endpoint is exported as an unmarked (non-sensitive) Terraform output, disclosing the reachable address of a publicly accessible database to anyone with access to state or CI logs.
